IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p95#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p95#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p95#2/r4.claim: The opening verses from Sād and the Qurʾān through their charge that this is fabrication were revealed about Quraysh in response to this episode.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p95#2/r4.anchor: فقالوا أجعل الآلهة إلها واحدا فنزلت فيهم ﴿ ص والقرآن ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ إن هذا إلا اختلاق ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r12.claim: Al-milla al-ākhira may mean Christianity, whose adherents did not teach Muhammad’s monotheism, or Quraysh’s inherited religion.

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r13.claim: Alternatively, the “later religion” means the religion of Quraysh’s own ancestors.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r13.anchor: أو يكون المراد بالمراد بالملة الآخرة ملة قريش

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r14.anchor: إن هاذا إلا اختلاق } افتعال وكذب

RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r15.claim: Their inference that monotheism is false because their ancestors never professed it exposes the invalidity of taqlīd: if following ancestors were sound, their polytheist argument would be sound.
RAZI-FULL:v26p155#2/r15.anchor: نحن ما سمعنا عن أسلافنا القول بالتوحيد

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r6.claim: Their reasoning, according to R, was that a message unheard of among their predecessors must be false.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r6.anchor: Their reasoning was that if they had not heard this message from their predecessors, then it must be something false (R).

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r7.claim: They therefore regarded the Qur'an as Muhammad's invention or fabrication, an accusation also made against Noah and Moses; the source points to Qur'anic responses to it.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r7.anchor: Thus to their minds the Quran must have been an invention or a fabrication by Muhammad (see 21:5; 25:4; 32:3;

STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.claim: The rejection of revelation by leaders and notables is discussed further at 34:34.
STUDYQURAN:38:4/r8.anchor: Regarding the tendency of leaders and notables to reject revelation, see 34:34c.

STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.speaker: IK, Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.claim: A report says Quraysh leaders complained to Abū Ṭālib; Muhammad asked only that they declare there is no god but God, promising Arab allegiance and non-Arab tribute, and they scoffed and said they would say ten declarations.
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r1.anchor: They had gone with the Prophet to his uncle and protector, Abū Ṭālib, to complain about the Prophet’s preaching.

STUDYQURAN:38:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r2.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r2.claim: Other accounts say this event occasioned the revelation of verses 1–7.
STUDYQURAN:38:5/r2.anchor: According to other accounts, this event occasioned the revelation of vv. 1–7 (IJ).

BURSEVI:v8p4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r2.claim: By this they mean the Prophet's teaching of God's oneness.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r2.anchor: ما سمعنا بهاذا} : الذي يقوله من التوحيد

BURSEVI:v8p4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r3.claim: The phrase is an adverbial attached to سمعنا and means the religion in which they found their forefathers, the Quraysh tradition that came later than previous religions.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r3.anchor: ظرف لغو سمعنا ؛ أي : في الملة التي أدركنا عليها آباءنا

BURSEVI:v8p4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r4.claim: Their appeal to inherited religion signals the ignorant reliance on custom and imitation of ancestral error instead of a sound path of worship.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى ركون الجهال إلى التقليد والعادة وما وجدوا عليه أسلافهم من الضلال

BURSEVI:v8p4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r5.claim: The cited Persian verse warns that a traveler may follow a route believing it leads to the Kaaba when it actually leads to Turkistan.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r5.anchor: ترسم نرسى بكعبه اي اعرابى كين ره كه توميروى بتركستانست

BURSEVI:v8p4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4/r6.claim: Milla, like din, properly means the law God prescribed through prophets so servants may attain His reward and nearness; applying it to polytheist custom is figurative by analogy.
BURSEVI:v8p4/r6.anchor: والملة كالدين اسم لما شرع الله لعباده على يد الأنبياء ليتوصلوا به إلى ثواب الله وجواره

BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r1.claim: Here إن is a negator equivalent to ما; اختلاق means a lie invented by the speaker himself.
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r1.anchor: إن هاذآ} : نافية بمعنى ما {إلا اختلاق}

BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says that when خلق describes speech, it means a lie; some therefore avoided applying the term خلق to the Quran.
BURSEVI:v8p4#2/r2.anchor: في "المفردات" : وكل موضع استعمل فيه الخلق

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the latter religion as Christianity; the reported view says Quraysh had not heard Muhammad's call to worship God alone or his scripture in that faith.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} [ص: 7] يقول: «النصرانية»

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says they argued that if the Quran were true, Christians would have told them about it.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r3.speaker: القرظي
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r3.claim: Al-Quraẓī glosses the latter religion as the religion of Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r3.anchor: عن القرظي في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r4.claim: Al-Suddī also identifies the latter religion as Christianity.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r4.anchor: عن السدي {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r5.claim: Another view from Mujahid takes it to mean that they had not heard this in the Quraysh religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r6.claim: Qatada understands it as their own religion and their own time: they had never heard this in their religion or era.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة}

TAB-FULL:v20p22/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says الآخرة means the other or later religion, while milla means religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p22/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.claim: Al-Suddī recounts Quraysh elders—Abu Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth—meeting to ask Abu Talib to stop Muhammad's criticism of their gods and leave each side to its worship; they feared Arab reproach if they attacked after his death.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r1.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم أبو جهل

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.claim: In al-Suddī's account, Muhammad told Abu Talib he called Quraysh to a word by which Arabs would submit and they would rule the non-Arabs; when he said “There is no god but God,” they rejected alternatives, left angrily, and threatened him.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r2.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.claim: At Abu Talib's deathbed, Muhammad urged him to profess that there is no god but God; Abu Talib declined lest Arabs say he feared death, and stayed with his forefathers' religion.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r3.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا

TAB-FULL:v20p24/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r4.claim: Al-Suddī's account says that after Abu Talib refused the profession of faith, the verse “You do not guide whom you love” (28:56) was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v20p24/r4.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r1.claim: The Quraysh claim that the Quran is اختلاق means it is a lie Muhammad fabricated and made up.
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r1.anchor: عن السدي، {إن هذا إلا اختلاق} [ص: 7] «اختلقه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses اختلاق as false conjecture or fabrication.
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses اختلاق as a lie.
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r4.claim: Qatada says it is something they make up.

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says it is something Muhammad fabricated.

TAB-FULL:v20p26/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says their claim means that this is only a lie.
TAB-FULL:v20p26/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

TABATABAI:38:7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:7/r4.claim: By the later religion they mean the religion followed by later peoples contemporary or near-contemporary to them, in contrast to ancient peoples' religions; they say this is absent from today's accepted religion and belongs only to ancient tales.
TABATABAI:38:7/r4.anchor: أرادوا بالملة الآخرة المذهب الذي تداوله الآخرون من الأمم المعاصرين لهم أو المقارنين لعصرهم قبال الملل الأولى

TABATABAI:38:7-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r1.claim: An alternative identifies the later religion as Christianity, the latest religion, which teaches Trinity rather than monotheism; the author rejects this because Christianity had little standing among them compared with Islam.
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r1.anchor: وقيل المراد بالملة الآخرة النصرانية لأنها آخر الملل وهم لا يقولون بالتوحيد بل بالتثليث

TABATABAI:38:7-10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r2.claim: اختلاق means a lie or fabrication.
TABATABAI:38:7-10/r2.anchor: إن هذا إلا اختلاق } أي كذب وافتعال

TABRISI:38:6-9/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r2.claim: Ikhtilaq, fabrication, is close in meaning to lying, slander, and false invention.

TABRISI:38:6-9/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:38:6-9/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says the last religion means Christianity, the latest religion, whose adherents do not profess God's oneness because they say He is three.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r14.anchor: يعنون في النصرانية لأنها آخر الملل عن ابن عباس قال إن النصارى لا يوحدون

TABRISI:38:6-9/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r15.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:38:6-9/r15.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take it to mean the religion of Quraysh in their own time.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r15.anchor: وقيل: يعنون ملة قريش أي في ملة زماننا هذا عن مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:38:6-9/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r16.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:38:6-9/r16.claim: Al-Hasan understands the phrase as saying they had not heard that this would happen at the end of time.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r16.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما سمعنا بأن هذا يكون في آخر الزمان عن الحسن

TABRISI:38:6-9/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:6-9/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:6-9/r17.claim: They call Muhammad's teaching a fabricated lie.
TABRISI:38:6-9/r17.anchor: { إلا اختلاق } أي تخرص وكذب وافتعال

THALABI:v8p178#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والقرظي والكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v8p178#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Qurazi, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say the later religion means Christianity because Christians associate another god with God.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس والقرظي والكلبي ومقاتل: يعنون النصرانية، لأن النصارى تجعل مع الله إلها

THALABI:v8p178#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v8p178#2/r14.claim: Mujahid and Qatada instead say it means Quraysh's religion of their present time.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: يعنون ملة قريش، ملة زماننا هذا

THALABI:v8p178#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p178#2/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p178#2/r15.claim: They call Muhammad's claim fabrication and ask why the Quran was sent down to him alone; God says they doubt His revelation.
THALABI:v8p178#2/r15.anchor: إن هذا إلا اختلاق أأنزل عليه الذكر القرآن من بيننا قال الله عز وجل: بل هم في شك من ذكري

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r1.claim: “This” means the Prophet's teaching, which they say they had not heard in the inherited religion of their forefathers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r1.anchor: ما سمعنا بهذا } الذي يقوله { في الملة الآخرة } فيما أدركنا عليه آباءنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r2.claim: Ikhtilaq means a fabrication, falsehood, and lie.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:38:7-9/r2.anchor: إن هذا إلا اختلاق } زور وكذب

ELMALILI:38:1-14/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r19.claim: He renders millat al-ākhira as the other or later religious community and identifies it here with Christianity, the latest community before Islam, which accepted the Trinity.
ELMALILI:38:1-14/r19.anchor: Biz bunu millet-i âhirede işitmedik “millet-i âhire” diğer millet, yahut sonraki millet demektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r6.claim: One view identifies the last scriptural religion they mean as Christianity, the pre-Islamic religion that accepted the Trinity; the commentary cites Tabari, Zamakhshari, Razi, and Shawkani for the alternatives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r6.anchor: İslâm’dan önceki son kitâbî din olan ve teslîs inancını benimseyen Hıristiyanlığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r7.claim: A different view takes the phrase to refer to the pagans’ own religion; the commentary cites Tabari, Zamakhshari, Razi, and Shawkani in reporting the disputed referent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r7.anchor: veya kendi putperestlik dinlerini kastettikleri yönünde farklı görüşler vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r8.claim: Another interpretation paraphrases the objection as saying they had heard nothing from Jews and Christians about Muhammad’s prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:38:5/r8.anchor: Aynı cümle, “Biz, yahudiler ve hıristiyanlardan Muhammed’in peygamberliğiyle ilgili bir şey duymadık” şeklinde de yorumlanmıştır

BAQILLANI:v1p18/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r1.claim: The Qur'an cannot have been altered or lost: God guaranteed its preservation, and the multitudes who memorized it across places and circumstances would have exposed any change.
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r1.anchor: وقد ضمن الله حفظ كتابه أن يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه أو من خلفه

BAQILLANI:v1p18/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r2.claim: The Qur'an's many distinct audiences memorized it for recitation, law, interpretation, eloquence, or scrutiny, making coordinated concealment or alteration implausible.
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r2.anchor: وكيف يجوز على أهل هذه الهمم المختلفة والآراء المتباينة - على كثرة أعدادهم واختلاف بلادهم وتفاوت أغراضهم

BAQILLANI:v1p18/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r3.claim: Even a single changed word in Imruʾ al-Qays would have been disowned despite poetry's lesser importance; alteration of the Qur'an, essential to prayer and law, is still less conceivable.
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r3.anchor: لو زيد فيه بيت أو نقص منه بيت لا بل لو غير فيه لفظ

BAQILLANI:v1p18/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r4.claim: Some opponents dismissed the revelation as fabricated, claiming they had not heard such a thing in the latest religion.
BAQILLANI:v1p18/r4.anchor: قول بعضهم ( ﴿ ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة إن هذا إلا اختلاق

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r1.claim: Reports about earlier unseen events are evidence for Muhammad's prophethood; the Qur'an stresses that he had not learned these events from prior scripture or witnesses.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r1.anchor: فبين وجه دلالته من إخباره بهذه الأمور الغائبة السالفة

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r2.claim: To establish that the Qur'an's order exceeds familiar styles, Bāqillānī says one must show that it is not poetry, sajʿ, or metrical speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r2.anchor: ومن ادعى ذلك لم يكن له بد من أن يصحح أنه ليس من قبيل الشعر ولا السجع ولا الكلام الموزون

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r3.speaker: كفار قريش
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r3.claim: Some Quraysh disbelievers classified the Qur'an as poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r3.anchor: لأن قوما من كفار قريش ادعوا أنه شعر

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r4.speaker: الملحدة
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r4.claim: Some heretics claimed that the Qur'an contains poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r4.anchor: ومن الملحدة من يزعم أن فيه شعرا

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r5.speaker: أهل الملة
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r5.claim: Some Muslims described the Qur'an as rhymed prose, though more eloquent than the sajʿ they knew.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r5.anchor: ومن أهل الملة من يقول إنه كلام مسجع إلا أنه أفصح مما قد اعتادوه من أسجاعهم

BAQILLANI:v1p49/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r6.claim: Others claimed the Qur'an was metrical speech, which would still place it within familiar forms of discourse.
BAQILLANI:v1p49/r6.anchor: ومنهم من يدعى أنه كلام موزون

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identified Sūrat al-Naṣr as the last revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ( ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله ﴾

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r5.speaker: عائشة
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha identified Sūrat al-Māʾida as the last revelation.

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r6.speaker: البراء بن عازب
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r6.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib identified Sūrat Barāʾa as the last revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r6.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب آخر ما أنزل سورة براءة

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identified the verse about the day people return to God as the last revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير آخر ما أنزل قوله تعالى ( ﴿ واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ﴾

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r8.speaker: السدي
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r8.claim: Al-Suddī identified the instruction to say 'God is sufficient for me' as the last revelation.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r8.anchor: وقال السدى آخر ما أنزل ( ﴿ فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت ﴾

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r9.claim: These reports can differ because each authority may have named the last passage he personally heard; disagreement over its placement is not disagreement over the Qur'an's source.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في مثل هذا خلاف وأن يكون كل واحد ذكر آخر ما سمع

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r10.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r10.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r10.claim: The Qur'an's style differs from the Prophet's ordinary speech as sharply as one man's sermon differs from another; its order is outside familiar speech patterns.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r10.anchor: لكان البون بين كلامه وبينه مثل ما بين خطبة وخطبة ينشئهما رجل واحد

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r11.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r11.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r11.claim: Recognizing distinctions among poetic and other speech forms requires reflection and acquired discernment, not automatic perception.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r11.anchor: ويحتاج في معرفة ذوق الشعر ووزنه والفرق بينه وبين غيره من الأوزان يحتاج إلى نظر وتأمل

BAQILLANI:v1p292/r12.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r12.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r12.claim: A proof remains valid even when believers disagree about how it demonstrates its conclusion, just as they differ over arguments for the world's origination.
BAQILLANI:v1p292/r12.anchor: قد يثبت الشيء دليلا وإن اختلفوا في وجه دلالة البرهان

BURHAN:v1p288/r18.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r18.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p288/r18.claim: Al-milla al-akhira is said to mean the first in Coptic; Copts call the first the last and the last the first.
BURHAN:v1p288/r18.anchor: ﴿ الملة الآخرة ﴾ أى الأولى بالقبطية والقبط يسمون الآخرة الأولى

BURHAN:v1p288/r27.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r27.speaker: الطبري
BURHAN:v1p288/r27.claim: Al-Tabari says apparent foreign parallels are words that Arabic, Persian, and Ethiopian speakers happened to share.
BURHAN:v1p288/r27.anchor: فقال الطبرى هذه الأمثلة المنسوبة إلى سائر اللغات إنما اتفق

BURHAN:v1p288/r28.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r28.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p288/r28.claim: Ibn Faris transmits the account of coincidentally shared words from Abu ʿUbayd.
BURHAN:v1p288/r28.anchor: وحكاه ابن فارس عن أبى عبيد

BURHAN:v1p288/r29.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r29.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v1p288/r29.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Arab trade and travel brought foreign terms into Arabic; Arabs adapted their sounds and used them in poetry and conversation until they became eloquent Arabic, the form in which the Qur'an came.
BURHAN:v1p288/r29.anchor: وقال ابن عطية بل كان للعرب العاربة التى نزل القرآن بلغتهم بعض مخالطة لسائر الألسن

BURHAN:v1p288/r30.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r30.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v1p288/r30.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says unfamiliarity with a term is like not knowing an openly foreign language, as Ibn Abbas did not know fatir; the terms were foreign in origin but naturalized and thus Arabic in use.
BURHAN:v1p288/r30.anchor: فإن جهلها عربى فكجهله الصريح بما فى لغة غيره

ITQAN:v2p397/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p397/r14.speaker: شيذلة
ITQAN:v2p397/r14.claim: Shidhla says al-milla al-akhira means the first pre-Islamic religion: Coptic calls “the latter” “the first,” and vice versa; al-Zarkashi cites this explanation.
ITQAN:v2p397/r14.anchor: الملة الآخرة قال شيذلة الجاهلية الأولى أي الآخرة في الملة الآخرة

ITQAN:v4p333/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p333/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p333/r3.claim: People derived timekeeping from verses about day and night, the sun and moon, their phases, stars and constellations.
ITQAN:v4p333/r3.anchor: ونظر قوم إلى ما فيه من الآيات الدالات على الحكم الباهرة

ITQAN:v4p333/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p333/r4.speaker: الكتاب والشعراء
ITQAN:v4p333/r4.claim: Writers and poets derived semantics and rhetorical sciences from Quranic eloquence, arrangement, context, openings, endings, shifts of address, expansion and concision.
ITQAN:v4p333/r4.anchor: ونظر الكتاب والشعراء إلى ما فيه من جزالة اللفظ وبديع النظم

ITQAN:v4p333/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p333/r5.speaker: أرباب الإشارات وأصحاب الحقيقة
ITQAN:v4p333/r5.claim: People of spiritual allusion and inner reality derived subtle senses and terms such as annihilation, abiding, presence, fear, awe, intimacy, estrangement, contraction and expansion.
ITQAN:v4p333/r5.anchor: ونظر فيه أرباب الإشارات وأصحاب الحقيقة فلاح لهم من ألفاظه معان ودقائق

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that during Abu Talib’s illness the Prophet asked Quraysh for one word, the declaration of God’s oneness; they objected, and the verses were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: مرض أبو طالب، فجاءت قريش وجاء النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.claim: Commentators recount that Quraysh, upset by Umar’s conversion, asked the Prophet to abandon his God and idols; they rejected his call to affirm one God, and these verses followed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p366/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما أسلم عمر بن الخطاب شق ذلك على قريش

DAMGHANI:v1p23/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r6.claim: Al-ākhira can mean the last or most recent one: the latest prior religious community, or the later of two promised punishments.
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r6.anchor: الرابع : الآخرة يعني الأخيرة . قوله تعالى

DAMGHANI:v1p162/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r5.claim: خلق can mean fabrication or lying, including a claim made up from oneself.
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r5.anchor: الثاني : الخلق يعني التخرص والكذب قوله سبحانه وتعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.claim: In these Qur'anic examples, خلق means fabrication and lying; the entry also cites the earlier nations' claim that the message was their custom.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخلق في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r1.claim: Al-ākhira is so named because it follows this world; al-ākhir is what has something before it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r1.anchor: الآخر : ما قبله سابق . وسميت الآخرة آخرة لأنها بعد الدنيا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r2.claim: Bi-ākhira means finally, akhariyāt al-nās the rear of a group, and the ākhira of a saddle its back part.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r2.anchor: وتقول : فعلت هذا بأخرة ، أي : أخيرا . وجاء فلان في أخريات الناس ، وآخرة : الرحل : مؤخره .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r3.claim: A Qurʾanic sense of al-ākhira is the Resurrection or Last Day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r3.anchor: أحدها : القيامة . ومنه قوله : [ تعالى في البقرة ] : ﴿ وبالآخرة هم يوقنون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r4.claim: Al-ākhira can mean Paradise, as in verses about reward and the lasting abode for the God-conscious.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r4.anchor: والثاني : الجنة . ومنه قوله [ تعالى في البقرة ] : ^ ( ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ماله في الآخرة من خلاق ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r5.claim: A third sense is Hell, illustrated by the worshipper who fears the Hereafter while hoping for his Lord’s mercy.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r5.anchor: والثالث : جهنم . ومنه قوله تعالى في الزمر : ^ ( أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r6.claim: Al-ākhira can refer to the grave, as in God’s promise to make believers firm in this life and the next.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r6.anchor: والرابع : القبر . ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم ^ ( يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r7.claim: This verse uses al-ākhira for the later religious community, the community of Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r7.anchor: والخامس : ملة عيسى عليه السلام . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة ص : ^ ( ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r8.claim: Al-ākhira can denote the final punishment or destruction of the Israelites.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p149/r8.anchor: والسادس : المرة الأخيرة من اهلاك بني إسرائيل . ومنه قوله تعالى في بني إسرائيل : ^ ( فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسؤوا وجوهكم ) ^

NAHHAS:v3p454/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r15.claim: اختلاق means fabrication or invention; خلق and اختلق can mean originating without a model.
NAHHAS:v3p454/r15.anchor: أي تكذيب وابتداع يقال خلق واختلق أي ابتدع

NAHHAS:v3p454/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p454/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p454/r16.claim: The author says their statement shows they are envious.

SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r1.claim: في الملة can modify سمعنا directly.
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق ب " سمعنا " أي: لم نسمع في الملة الآخرة بهذا الذي جئت به.

SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r2.claim: Alternatively it is an omitted circumstantial phrase describing هذا.
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه متعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من هذا أي: ما سمعنا بهذا كائنا في الملة الآخرة.

SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r3.claim: They claim no soothsayer or scriptural community spoke of God's oneness in the later religion; al-Samin calls this extreme lying.
SAMIN-DURR:38:7/r3.anchor: أي: لم نسمع من الكهان ولا من أهل الكتب أنه يحدث توحيد الله في الملة الآخرة، وهذا من فرط كذبهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r3.claim: The leaders claim they had heard nothing like this in Christianity, Judaism, or the tradition they inherited from their fathers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r3.anchor: أي ما سمعنا بهذا في النصرانية ولا اليهودية ولا فيما أدركنا عليه آباءنا

ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r4.claim: Ikhtilāq here means a fabrication or false assertion.
ZAJJAJ:v4p321/r4.anchor: (إن هذا إلا اختلاق). أي إلا تقول

ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n10/r1.claim: Asad reads "faiths of latter days" as faiths prevalent in his own time, alluding to Christianity's Trinity and other beliefs in multiple or incarnate divine powers, including Hinduism's triad.
ASAD-NOTES:38:6#n10/r1.anchor: I.e., "in any of the faiths prevalent in our days": an oblique reference to Christianity and its dogma of the Trinity

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r1.claim: One explanation says disconnected letters catch attention better than meaningful words: listeners do not mistake them for the whole statement and keep listening for what follows.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r1.anchor: السامع أنه كل المقصود ولا كلام بعد ذلك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r2.speaker: الإمام الجويني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r2.claim: Al-Juwayni endorses the letters as attention signals: the Qur'an's valuable meanings require alert hearing, and unfamiliar sounds suit revelation better than ordinary interjections.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r2.anchor: استجاده الإمام الجويني، أبو المعالي عبد الملك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r3.claim: Some identify the letters with abjad numerals and use them to calculate the duration of the Muslim community, earlier peoples, or the world.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r3.anchor: ويعنون به الأبجدية: أبجد هوز حطي كلمن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r4.claim: She tentatively traces the numerical-letter reports to the story of the Jewish Huyayy ibn Akhtab, which Ibn Ishaq recounts amid accounts of Jewish plotting and disputation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p145/r4.anchor: تبدأ من قصة "حُيَىَّ بن أخطب اليهودي" وقد نقلها "ابن إسحاق" مفصلة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.claim: Like the previous sūrahs in this group, Ṣād is founded on tawḥīd; Quraysh oppose its reminder from arrogance and polytheism and will believe only when it is too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r1.anchor: Like the previous sūrahs of this group, this sūrah is also based on tawh@īd.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.claim: Verses 1–11 present the Qur’an as a reminder rejected from arrogance, paralleling earlier nations; Quraysh too will believe only after seeing their fate, when faith is useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r2.anchor: This Qur’ān is a reminder for people; however, because of arrogance and haughtiness they are opposing it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.claim: Quraysh cannot accept a messenger from among themselves, so they call him sorcerer and liar; their leaders rally people to defend idols and ancestral religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p475/r3.anchor: They are not able to digest the fact that a person from among them, as God’s messenger, should warn them of the fate of polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r1.claim: The Qur’an recounts that all prophets from Noah to Abraham preached pure monotheism, while Abraham’s and Ishmael’s history and the Kaaba explain the Arabs’ true origins.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r1.anchor: all prophets of God from Noah (sws) to Abraham (sws) preached the pure message of tawh@īd.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r2.claim: Abraham and Ishmael settled their descendants in Arabia to serve Islam and preach monotheism; the Kaaba was built for that purpose, but Quraysh filled it with idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r2.anchor: The house of God – whose custodianship is currently in the hands of Quraysh – was also built for this purpose.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r3.claim: The Qur’anic history struck at Quraysh’s claims and offered them no persuasive answer; stubbornly, they said their later history lacked monotheism and called the account fabricated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r3.anchor: This history narrated by the Qur’ān was a heavy blow to the claims of the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r4.claim: They argue that if this account of Arab history were true, their forefathers would have transmitted some trace of it; instead, they follow and will continue their inherited religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r4.anchor: they have never heard the message of tawh@īd in this later part of their history

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r5.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r5.claim: Some identify the ‘later religion’ with the Christian nation, but Islahi rejects this for lack of contextual support; it would matter only if Quraysh believed in Christianity or Muhammad based his call on it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p482/r5.anchor: Some people are of the opinion that ِةَّلِمْال ِةَرِخ ْلَآا refers to the Christian nation; however, no contextual indication for this exists.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses “the latter community” as Christianity.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله ﴿ بهذا في الملة الآخرة ﴾ قال النصرانية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r2.claim: Qatāda says “the latter community” means the religion the speakers themselves follow.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p160#3/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة هو الدين الذي نحن عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r16.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب، ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r16.claim: These authorities take الملة الآخرة as the Christians' religion, which includes trinitarian belief rather than unification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p138/r16.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، ومحمد بن كعب، ومقاتل: ملة النصارى، لأن فيها التثليث، ولا توحد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r1.claim: In “we have not heard of this,” “this” refers to what Muhammad is saying.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب ومقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and Muqatil take the last community to mean the Christians; “last” describes their belief, since they do not accept Muhammad's prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب ومقاتل أرادوا ملة النصارى والتوصيف بالآخرة الإعتقاد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r3.claim: On the Christian reading, they mean they heard the opposite of monotheism: Christians professed a trinity and claimed it was Jesus' religion, a claim Alusi rejects on Jesus' behalf.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r3.anchor: ومرادهم من قولهم ما سمعنا الخ أنا سمعنا خلافه وهو عدم التوحيد فإن النصارى كانوا يثلثون

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r4.claim: Mujahid and Qatada also take the phrase to mean the Arabs' religion and custom, inherited from their fathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r4.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا وقتادة أرادوا ملة العرب ونحلتها التي أدركوا عليها آباءهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r5.claim: An alternative parsing makes “in the last community” circumstantial from the demonstrative “this,” rather than governed by “we heard”; the claim then concerns the end-time community's monotheistic religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون في الملة الآخرة حالا من اسصم الإشارة لا متعلقا بسمعنا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r6.claim: On that parsing, they claim scripture people and soothsayers had not foretold a monotheist end-time prophet; Alusi says this is a lie, since his idol-breaking call to worship God was widely known before his appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r6.anchor: ولقد كذبوا في ذلك فإن حديث إن النبي المبعوث آخر الزمان يكسر الأصنام ويدعو إلى توحيد الملك العلام كان أشهر الأمور قبل الظهور

ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r7.claim: “Fabrication” means an invention and falsehood with no precedent or model.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p167#2/r7.anchor: أي افتعال وافتراء من غير سبق مثل له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say “the last religion” means Christianity, the latest religion, whose adherents do not affirm unity but say “three of three.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، والكلبي، ومقاتل: يعنون النصرانية، لأنها آخر الملل وهم لا يوحدون،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r2.claim: Mujahid and Qatada instead say it refers to the Quraysh religion and the faith they follow.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: يعنون ملة قريش ودينهم الذي هم عليه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p72#2/r3.claim: Ikhtilaq means a lie and fabrication.

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r1.claim: They mean the doctrine of one God that Muhammad teaches.

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r2.claim: The phrase may mean the inherited religion in which their ancestors lived, or the last prior religion, Christianity, whose adherents teach a Trinity; alternatively it describes a prospective religion in which neither scriptural scholars nor soothsayers heard of monotheism.
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r2.anchor: في الملة التي أدركنا عليها آباءنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:38:7-8/r3.claim: They call the claim a fabrication.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r11.claim: Restricting their claim to the “last religion” implies they knew monotheism in the earlier tradition, including Abraham and his descendants before ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy, and had also known resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r11.anchor: وتقييدهم لها يدل على أنهم عالمون به في الملة الأولى , وأنهم عارفون بأن إبراهيم عليه السلام ومن وجد من أولاده الذين هم آباؤهم إلى عمرو بن لحي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r12.speaker: ابن الفرات
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r12.claim: Ibn al-Furāt recounts Hujr ibn ʿAmr’s campaign against Banū Asad and their displacement to Tihāma as historical context for the cited Arab account.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r12.anchor: ذكر ابن الفرات في تأريخه يوم حليمة من أيام العرب وقال : إن حجر بن عمرو آكل المرار سار إلى بني أسد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r13.speaker: عبيد بن الأبرص
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r13.claim: The cited verse says the displaced people became servants until the Resurrection, serving as poetic evidence that Arabs knew of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r13.anchor: فقال عبيد بن الأبرص من أبيات : ومنعتهم نجدا فقد حلوا على وحل تهامه أنت المليك عليهم وهم العبيد إلى القيامه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r14.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r14.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the first to release protected grazing animals and worship idols was ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir of Khuzāʿa, whom the Prophet saw dragged through Hell by his entrails.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r14.anchor: وروى الإمام أحمد عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( إن أول من سيب السوايب وعبد الأصنام أبو خزاعة عمرو بن عامر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r15.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r15.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy ibn Qumayʿa as the first to alter Abraham’s religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r15.anchor: وروى الطبراني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( أول من غير دين إبراهيم عليه السلام عمرو بن لحي بن قميئة )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r16.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r16.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet removed images showing Abraham and Ishmael with divining arrows and said they had never used such arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r16.anchor: وروى البخاري في فتح مكة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r17.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r17.claim: Anas reports that a man was told his father was in Hell; as he turned away, the Prophet called him back and said that both his father and the Prophet’s father were in Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r17.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن رجلا قال : يا رسول الله ! أين أبي ! قال ( في النار , فلما قفى دعاه فقال : إن أبي وأباك في النار )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r18.claim: These reports refute the claim that people of the interval were ignorant in a way that absolved them; the earlier discussion in al-Isrāʾ also bears on the issue.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p359/r18.anchor: فبطل ما يقال من أن أهل الفترة جهلوا جهلا أسقط عنهم اللوم , ويؤيده ما في الصحيح عن أنس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r1.claim: The verse in al-Naḥl says every community received a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of idols, and people were judged as guided or astray.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r1.anchor: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدو الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r2.claim: Not having heard a doctrine in a given tradition does not make it fabrication; reflection readily reveals the meaning of monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r2.anchor: لا ملازمة بين عدم سماعهم فيها وبين كونه اختلافا , بل هو قول يعرف معانيه بأدنى تأمل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s account of Abū Ṭālib’s illness says the Prophet asked Quraysh for one word, “There is no god but God”; they objected with these verses. Al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p361/r3.anchor: والطبري وابن أبي حاتم وغيرهم عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : مرض أبو طالب فجاءته قريش

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r6.claim: Mujahid says “the latter community” means Christianity; the Quraysh claimed Christians would have told them if the Quran were true.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r6.anchor: وفي قوله {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} قال: النصرانية قالوا: لو كان هذا القرآن حقا

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb interprets “the latter community” as the community of Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} قال: ملة عيسى عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r8.claim: Qatada interprets “the latter community” as Christianity.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} قال: النصرانية

DURR-FULL:v7p145/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r9.claim: Qatada says they meant this was neither in their religion nor their time, and that the Quran was merely something fabricated.
DURR-FULL:v7p145/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} أي في ديننا هذا ولا في زماننا هذا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r1.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says “the latter religion” means the religion of Jesus.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الاخرة قال : ملة عيسى عليه السلام .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies “the latter religion” as Christianity.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3236#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الاخرة قال : النصرانية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r3.claim: The ‘this’ in their denial refers to the same claim in the preceding accusation, namely making the many gods one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r3.anchor: والإشارة إلى ما أشير إليه بقولهم : { إن هاذا لشيء يراد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r4.claim: The sentence may stand independently or explain their claim that the matter is contrived, since saying they had never heard it shows they considered it invented.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r4.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة أو مبينة لجملة { إن هاذا لشيء يراد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r5.claim: Repeating the demonstrative instead of using a pronoun further distinguishes the claim; bi-hādhā has an omitted ‘like,’ meaning something like this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r5.anchor: وإعادة اسم الإشارة من وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر لقصد زيادة تمييزه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r6.claim: Their report of never having heard this is a rhetorical way to express rejection and accuse the claim of falsehood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r6.anchor: ونفي السماع هنا خبر مستعمل كناية عن الاستبعاد والاتهام بالكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r7.claim: Milla means religion, as shown by the verses about following the Jews’ and Christians’ religion and about the religion of Joseph’s forefathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r7.anchor: و { الملة } : الدين ، قال تعالى : { ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r8.claim: Ākhira is the feminine of ākhir, the one that comes after a period in which similar instances have been established, as in the later creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r8.anchor: و { الآخرة } : تأنيث الآخر وهو الذي يكون بعد مضي مدة تقررت فيها أمثاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r9.claim: The prepositional phrase may be a circumstantial modifier of the demonstrative and attached to ‘heard’: they have never heard this before now, so do not accept it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r9.anchor: والمجرور من قوله : { في الملة الآخرة } يجوز أن يكون ظرفا مستقرا في موضع الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأصحابه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and his associates take the ‘last religion’ to mean Christianity; the polytheists invoked its plurality of gods against monotheism, and their denial of hearing this implies the opposite had been heard.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r11.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean the Quraysh religion; at Abū Ṭālib’s deathbed the Prophet urged him to profess God’s oneness, while the chiefs asked whether he would abandon ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p212/r11.anchor: فقالوا له جميعا : أترغب عن ملة عبد المطلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r1.claim: The sentence explains “we never heard of this” and sums up the chiefs’ preceding exhortation to persist with their gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r1.anchor: وهذا هو المتحصل من كلامهم المبدوء ب { امشوا واصبروا على ءالهتكم } فهذه الجملة كالفذلكة لكلامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r2.claim: Ikhtilāq is fabricated falsehood for which its speaker has no plausible grounds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p213/r2.anchor: والاختلاق : الكذب المخترع الذي لا شبهة لقائله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r11.claim: By saying they had not heard of this, they mean the claim that God is one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r11.anchor: وقولهم: ما سمعنا بهذا يريدون بمثل هذه المقالة أن الإله واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r12.claim: Mujahid says the last religion means the religion and tradition followed by the Arabs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r12.anchor: فقال مجاهد: أرادوا ملتهم ونحلتهم التي العرب عليها، ويقال لكل ما تتبعه أمة ما ملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi identify it as Christianity, a religion known for the Trinity and for denying that God is one; the author considers this apt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي: أراد ملة النصارى، وذلك متجه، لأنها ملة شهير فيها التثليث، وأن الإله ليس بواحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r14.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r14.claim: Another group reads the phrase as referring to the latter religion expected at the end of time: before Muhammad, people anticipated a prophet and a new religion, as supported by reports about monks, Shiq and Satih, and Israelite expectations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p493#2/r14.anchor: وقالت فرقة معنى قولهم: ما سمعنا أنه يكون مثل هذا، ولا أنه يقال في الملة الآخرة التي كنا نسمع أنها تكون في آخر الزمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p494/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p494/r1.claim: They call all that Muhammad reports from God a fabrication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p494/r1.anchor: وقولهم: إن هذا إلا اختلاق إشارة إلى جميع ما يخبر به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r1.claim: The thing they say they have not heard before is Muhammad's teaching of monotheism.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ ما سمعنا بهذا ﴾ الذي جاء به محمد من التوحيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومحمد بن كعب القرظي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r2.claim: One view takes the later religious community to mean Christians; Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and Muqatil are cited for it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r2.anchor: أحدها النصرانية رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وإبراهيم بن المهاجر عن مجاهد وبه قال محمد بن كعب القرظي ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r3.claim: A second view takes the phrase to mean the religion of Quraysh; Mujahid and Qatada are cited.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنها ملة قريش رواه ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد وبه قال قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj say the phrase includes Judaism and Christianity: Jews associated Uzayr with God and Christians said three are one.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r4.anchor: والثالث اليهودية والنصرانية قاله الفراء والزجاج والمعنى أن اليهود أشركت بعزير والنصارى قالت ثالث ثلاثة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p103#2/r5.claim: Ikhtilāq here means a lie or fabrication.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi understand the last religion as Christianity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r11.anchor: أحدها : في النصرانية لأنها كانت آخر الملل , قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r12.speaker: الحكم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r12.claim: Al-Hakam means the period between Jesus and Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r12.anchor: الثاني : فيما بين عيسى ومحمد عليهما السلام , قاله الحكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r13.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r13.anchor: الثالث : في ملة قريش , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r14.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r14.claim: Al-Hasan reads it as saying it had not arisen in their own time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r14.anchor: الرابع : معناه أننا ما سمعنا أنه يخرج ذلك في زماننا , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r15.claim: They accuse Muhammad of fabricating a lie.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p78/r15.anchor: أي كذب اختلقه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the “later community” means Quraysh's religion.
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة ﴾ يعنون ملة قريش

MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses ikhtilāq as a lie.
MUJAHID:v2p547#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إن هذا إلا اختلاق ﴾ قال الاختلاق الكذب

MUQATIL:38:7-10/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r1.claim: The last religion means Christianity, the latest religious community, whose adherents claim that Jesus son of Mary is alongside God.
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r1.anchor: { ما سمعنا بهذا } الأمر الذى يقول محمد { فى الملة الآخرة } يعنى ملة النصرانية، وهى آخر الملل

MUQATIL:38:7-10/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r2.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r2.claim: Al-Walīd called the Quran a fabrication that Muhammad made up on his own.
MUQATIL:38:7-10/r2.anchor: ثم قال الوليد: { إن هذا } القرآن { إلا اختلاق } [آية: 7] من محمد تقوله من تلقاء نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r1.claim: What they had not heard of is monotheism.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r2.claim: One view takes the last religion to mean Christianity, latest among religious communities, whose adherents are trinitarian rather than unitarian.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r2.anchor: فى ملة عيسى التى هى آخر الملل لأن النصارى مثلثة غير موحدة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, they mean Quraysh's religion inherited from their fathers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r3.anchor: أو فى ملة قريش التى أدركنا عليها آباءنا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r4.claim: They call the claim a lie fabricated by Muhammad himself.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p33#2/r4.anchor: كذب اختلقه محمد من تلقاء نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r1.claim: The opening praise describes God as beyond imaginative indication and rational comprehension, eternal beyond created limits, and uniquely divine before and after all that exists.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r1.anchor: المنزه بذاته عن إشارة الأوهام المقدس بصفاته عن إدراك العقول والأفهام المتصف بالألوهية قبل كل موجود الباقي بالنعوت السرمدية بعد كل محدود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r2.claim: God is unlike created beings, bodies, and humanity, does not occupy space, and is powerful and sovereign beyond challenge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r2.anchor: القديم الذي تعالى عن مماثلة الحدثان العظيم الذى تنزه عن مماسة المكان المتعالى عن مضاهاة الأجسام ومشابهة الأنام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r3.claim: The preface praises God as all-knowing, creator and teacher of humanity, and wise in revealing the Qur'an as a cure for souls and bodies.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r3.anchor: العليم الذي خلق الانسان وعلمه البيان الحكيم الذى نزل القرآن شفاء للأرواح والأبدان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r4.claim: At a request, al-Nasafī says he wrote a moderate tafsir integrating grammar, readings, rhetorical subtleties, and allusions, presenting Sunni views and excluding innovators' doctrines.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r4.anchor: كتابا وسطا في التأويلات جامعا لوجوه الاعراب والقراءات متضمنا لدقائق علمى البديع والاشارات حاليا بأقاويل أهل السنة والجماعة خاليا عن أباطيل أهل البدع والضلالة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r5.claim: He says he hesitated from awareness of human limits and caution, then completed the work quickly with God's aid and titled it Madārik al-tanzīl wa-ḥaqāʾiq al-taʾwīl.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p1/r5.anchor: وكنت أقدم فيه رجلا وأؤخر أخرى استقصارا لقوة البشر عن درك هذا الوطر

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والقرظي وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Qurazi, Qatada, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, and al-Suddi take the last religion to mean Christianity, whose adherents associate another god with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس والقرظي وقتادة ومقاتل والكلبي والسدي: يعنون ملة عيسى النصرانية

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r12.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r12.claim: Mujahid and, in another report, Qatada say the phrase means the religion of Quraysh.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة أيضا: يعنون ملة قريش.

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r13.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r13.claim: Al-Hasan understands them to mean that they had never heard such a thing would happen at the end of time.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما سمعنا أن هذا يكون في آخر الزمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r14.claim: Another explanation is that they had not heard from the People of the Book that Muhammad was a true messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r14.anchor: وقيل: أي ما سمعنا من أهل الكتاب أن محمدا رسول حق.

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain ikhtilāq as a lie or fabrication; khalaqa and ikhtalaqa mean to invent.

QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r16.claim: The related verb is also used of God creating creatures by originating them without a prior model.
QURTUBI-FULL:38:6-8/r16.anchor: وخلق الله عز وجل الخلق من هذا أي ابتدعهم على غير مثال

TIRMIDHI:3232/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3232/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:3232/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that during Abu Talib’s illness the Prophet asked Quraysh to profess one God, promising Arab allegiance and non-Arab jizya; they refused. Tirmidhi links their response to Ṣād 38:2–7 and grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
TIRMIDHI:3232/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ مَرِضَ أَبُو طَالِبٍ فَجَاءَتْهُ قُرَيْشٌ
